title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly check-in for the Redwood Private VPC pilot. Covered recent networking fixes, routing issues causing timeouts for the inference control plane, a plan for the runtime upgrade this Friday, and security/KMS confirmation for encryption at rest. Identified one blocker (NAT gateway session limits) and agreed on tests for end-to-end latency and canary traffic routing. Next steps: Redwood to share upgraded runtime image and deployment playbook, customer to validate VPC peering and provide network flow logs, schedule dry-run on Friday at 03:00 UTC.
next_steps: Redwood: share runtime image + upgrade playbook (Alex) by 2027-11-05
DataWave: collect VPC flow logs and validate peering (Liam) by 2027-11-05
Security: Evan to confirm KMS key rotation policy and required audit fields by 2027-11-06
Schedule Friday dry-run (Redwood + DataWave) for 2027-11-05 03:00 UTC
action_items: Alex Morgan - Upload runtime image to customer registry and send playbook - due 2027-11-05
Priya Shah - Provide test scripts for latency and KV cache warmup - due 2027-11-05
Liam O'Connor - Share VPC flow logs and current NAT gateway config - due 2027-11-05
Evan Zhang - Confirm KMS integration steps and required audit fields - due 2027-11-06
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Sofia Martinez: Sofia here. CTO.
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Liam, platform.
[00:09] Evan Zhang: Evan, security.
[00:11] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood, joining.
[00:13] Alex Morgan: Awesome. Agenda today: networking updates, routing errors we've been seeing, runtime upgrade this Friday, and security sign-off.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick update from our side, we ran the peering test yesterday. most things look fine but after about 12k concurrent sessions our NAT gateway started dropping state, causing some control plane calls to time out to the private control endpoint. might be config or AWS session limits.
[01:40] Priya Shah: okay that matches what we saw in the logs, calls from the agent to the runtime started 502-ing when session table overflowed. sounds like NAT connection tracking. did you have a spare NAT or are you using a single NAT?
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: single NAT right now for the pilot cluster, we can add a second but wanted to check if there's a config we should change on the Redwood side to reduce long-lived connections.
[02:27] Priya Shah: yeah we have a setting to use shorter keepalives and more aggressive connection reuse on the serving runtime; we'll push a config tweak. also, we can enable our routing policy to use shorter-lived proxied connections to the control plane.
[02:48] Alex Morgan: for context, the production rollout will use multiple NATs + autoscale but for pilot we missed that, so it's on us to make the runtime more NAT-friendly.
[03:10] Sofia Martinez: are there security implications to changing keepalives or connection reuse? Evan?
[03:20] Evan Zhang: not really, but we need to ensure session logging and source IP visibility remains intact for audit. if connections are pooled we need mapping in the logs.
[03:40] Priya Shah: noted, we'll ensure the agent includes source metadata and that logs are forwarded.
[04:00] Alex Morgan: next, routing — Priya can you summarize the intermittent 504s we saw last week?
[04:12] Priya Shah: yeah so between 10:00 and 11:30 UTC on Tuesday we had a spike in request TTL and some requests routed to a warm instance that then hit a model load stall. the model load stall seems tied to kernel selection heuristics when sequence length jumped on a small subset of requests — the runtime tried a vectorized path and fell back causing a ~6s stall.
[04:45] Liam O'Connor: hmm we do send mixed seq lengths, that's probably it. is there a way to pin model variant or force quantized path for the pilot until we patch?
[04:58] Priya Shah: yes we can pin to the quantized variant and disable the aggressive kernel selector for the pilot. that's a config toggle. we'll send the exact flag.
[05:15] Alex Morgan: good. Also Priya, you mentioned KV cache warmup earlier in the spike notes?
[05:22] Priya Shah: right, if the KV cache isn't warmed for a model shard new sessions incur a load penalty — about 200-300ms per new model activation. We'll provide a warmup script that hits prefix sequences and primes the KV. for canary traffic we'll run that before rolling.
[05:45] Sofia Martinez: perfect. that helps explain the tail latency we saw.
[06:02] Evan Zhang: Security questions — we got the KMS integration doc and did an initial pass. main ask: can we rotate keys without downtime and will Redwood surface key IDs in audit logs?
[06:18] Priya Shah: yes rotation is supported; the control plane will accept both old and new key IDs during rollover and we write key_id metadata to every resource event in the audit log. we'll send the audit field spec.
[06:40] Alex Morgan: also to confirm, logs are pushed to your S3 bucket via our delivery agent or you can pull from our audit API — which do you prefer?
[06:53] Evan Zhang: push to S3 with SNS notification is ideal. we already have SIEM ingestion from S3.
[07:02] Priya Shah: we'll enable S3 delivery and SNS notifications in the playbook.
[07:20] Liam O'Connor: timeline for the runtime upgrade? you mentioned Friday?
[07:26] Alex Morgan: yes target Friday 03:00 UTC for the dry-run upgrade; we want to run canary at 10% traffic then failover back if anything looks off.
[07:36] Sofia Martinez: is there a rollback plan?
[07:40] Priya Shah: full rollback path included — we'll snapshot runtime configs and can re-point the routing policy to the previous image. KV cache will be dropped on rollback but we'll re-warm.
[08:00] Liam O'Connor: is there an expected latency improvement with the upgrade?
[08:05] Priya Shah: we expect 10-18% p95 improvement for the quantized path and better CPU utilization on the serving nodes. but we'll validate with the test scripts.
[08:20] Alex Morgan: about canary routing — we'll set policy to route by region and by customer tag, and if error rate > 1% for 5 minutes we auto-fallback. sound good?
[08:32] Liam O'Connor: yes. one more ask: can we control the model variants the canary uses? we want canary on a lower-cost quantized variant not the full FP model.
[08:42] Priya Shah: yes the rollout config allows model variant pinning. we'll include examples in the playbook.
[09:05] Sofia Martinez: earlier you mentioned NAT session limits, is adding a second NAT sufficient or should we move to EKS with ENI trunking?
[09:18] Liam O'Connor: we could do ENI trunking but that's a bigger ops lift. second NAT + adjust keepalives is fastest.
[09:28] Priya Shah: agree. for the pilot second NAT + config changes is low risk. we'll verify with your flow logs.
[09:40] Alex Morgan: security again — any blockers from SOC2 side for the pilot?
[09:46] Evan Zhang: we need assurance around log retention, SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC, and the KMS integration detail; otherwise pilot is fine. we'll want the security whitepaper and SOC2 doc.
[10:02] Priya Shah: we'll share SOC2, ISO certs, and an internal security checklist tonight.
[10:12] Alex Morgan: good. Let's talk test plan: Priya, what will you run in the Friday dry-run?
[10:20] Priya Shah: sequence: 1) snapshot current deployment, 2) deploy upgrade to canary nodes (10%), 3) run workload generator with mixed seq lengths for 30 minutes, 4) collect p50/p95/p99 and error rates, 5) check KV cache hit ratios and agent connection counts. we'll provide the generator and expected thresholds.
[10:46] Liam O'Connor: we'll provide environment variables for the generator and open a port for the traffic.
[10:52] Priya Shah: great. I'll share the generator config and a script to run.
[11:05] Alex Morgan: any loose ends?
[11:08] Sofia Martinez: only that we want to validate audit fields include key_id and source_ip.
[11:13] Evan Zhang: yes and time sync — ensure NTP across nodes.
[11:20] Priya Shah: will include both in the playbook.
[11:35] Alex Morgan: recap: Redwood to send runtime image + playbook + test scripts; DataWave to share VPC flow logs and NAT config; security to confirm KMS key rotation details; schedule dry-run Friday 03:00 UTC.
[11:55] Sofia Martinez: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[12:00] Alex Morgan: thanks, we'll follow up in email.
[44:30] call ended
